title: Last Cigarette Ever
cn: 第 11 集 · 最后一支烟
novel:
The whole gang smoked — secretly, guiltily, in back alleys and on [[rooftops|rooftop]]. They all promised it would be their [[last cigarette|last cigarette]] ever. It never was.

Robin [[craved|crave]] one after every argument. Ted lit up when he was writing. Marshall sneaked one before bed. Barney smoked to look [[cool|cool]].

One day they made a [[pact|pact]]. "We quit together," Lily said. "No [[excuses|excuse]]."

The first hours were [[agony|agony]]. Marshall [[snapped|snap]] at a coworker. Ted could not [[concentrate|concentrate]]. Robin lay on the floor, [[muttering|mutter]] about [[nicotine|nicotine]].

By midnight, they had all failed — except Lily, who had never smoked at all. She watched them with quiet [[amusement|amusement]].

Future Ted would later reveal that this was indeed the last cigarette for each of them, though it took years. Some [[vices|vice]], he learned, were not [[defeated|defeat]] by willpower alone, but by time, by patience, and by the slow [[fading|fade]] of a habit that once felt like a friend.

rooftop.en: the top of a building where you can stand

excuse.en: a reason given to explain a failure

agony.en: great pain of body or mind

snap.en: to speak sharply because you are angry

concentrate.en: to focus your mind on something

nicotine.en: the drug in tobacco that makes you want more

amusement.en: the feeling of finding something funny

vice.en: a bad habit that harms you

fade.en: to slowly become weaker and disappear
